ānantarika:
[(1)anantara+ṇika.(2)anantarāya-ki]  CL=7 (1) (A) One who is immediately near or proximate in connection or effect. (B) The fruition (phala dhamma) of mental stability (cetosamādhi) that arises immediately following the attainment of magga dhamma. (C) The cetosamādhiphala dhamma that inevitably and immediately arises as the result following magga dhamma. (D) The paṭisandhi (rebirth linking) in hell, which occurs as an immediate result following death due to one of the five ānantarika kamma (actions with immediate results, such as matricide). (2)
The five ānantarika kamma (actions with immediate results, such as matricide, parricide, killing an arahant, injuring the Buddha, or causing a schism in the Sangha) unavoidably lead to rebirth in hell. No other kamma can obstruct or mitigate this result. (3) A person who performs any of the five ānantarika kamma experiences immediate rebirth in hell due to the unavoidably severe consequences of these actions.
